stem.en: Kabir says an egg is a single cell and it is huge, "so cells can be big". What does the yolk show?

text.en: A yolk is a store, not working cell material. It barely burns anything. The living part of an egg is a thin disc on top of the yolk, small enough for diffusion to feed it.
Cells can be big if they are round.

feedback.en: Round is the worst shape for surface per volume. The egg gets away with it by being mostly inert store.
A hen's egg begins as one cell. The exception is real; it works because almost none of the cell's volume is doing chemistry.

text.en: Eggs have holes in the shell.

feedback.en: Air does get through the shell, to the thin living disc. That disc is the size rule obeyed, not broken.

explanation.en: When a rule seems broken, ask what is really burning. In an egg, almost nothing, until the living part has grown into thousands of small cells.
